extracted.intended_audience: acute care hospitals (CJR‑X participants), hospital compliance officers, Medicare program administrators, and entities that collaborate or contract with CJR‑X participants
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and operational criteria for hospitals participating in the CMS Comprehensive Care for Joint Replacement Expansion (CJR‑X) Model, including definitions, participation rules, pricing/reconciliation procedures, quality measures, reporting and notification obligations, and data/documentation retention obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of capped retrospective trend factor to reconciliation target prices
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS applies the capped retrospective trend factor to the previously calculated normalized, risk adjusted target prices specific to each region and MS‑DRG/HCPCS episode type to calculate the reconciliation target prices, which are compared to performance year spending at reconciliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For episodes with anchor hospitalization or anchor procedure end dates in the fourth quarter of a performance year, the capped retrospective trend factor is applied specific to each assigned first and second fiscal year MS‑DRG/HCPCS episode type and region combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance year quality measures and baseline periods (Performance Year 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For performance year 4, specific measures apply with designated CQS baseline periods: (i) Hybrid Hospital‑Wide All‑Cause Readmission Measure (CMIT ID #356) with July 1, 2026–June 30, 2027 baseline; (ii) Hospital Harm—Falls with Injury (CMIT ID #1518) with CY 2028 baseline; (iii) Hospital Harm—Postoperative Respiratory Failure (CMIT ID #1788) with CY 2028 baseline; (iv) Thirty‑day Risk‑Standardized Death Rate among Surgical Inpatients with Complications (ISCMR) (CMIT ID #134) with July 1, 2025–June 30, 2027 baseline; (v) For LEJR episodes: THA/TKA PRO‑PM (CMIT ID #1618) with July 1, 2026–July 30, 2027 baseline; (vi) For LEJR and Spinal Fusion episodes: Information Transfer PRO‑PM (CMIT ID #1797) with CY 2028 baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These measures and their baseline periods are used to compute the Composite Quality Score (CQS) for PY4 as specified at §512.547.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance year quality measures and baseline periods (Performance Year 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For performance year 5, specific measures apply with designated CQS baseline periods: (i) Hybrid Hospital‑Wide All‑Cause Readmission Measure (CMIT ID #356) with July 1, 2027–June 30, 2028 baseline; (ii) Hospital Harm—Falls with Injury (CMIT ID #1518) with CY 2029 baseline; (iii) Hospital Harm—Postoperative Respiratory Failure (CMIT ID #1788) with CY 2029 baseline; (iv) Thirty‑day Risk‑Standardized Death Rate among Surgical Inpatients with Complications (ISCMR) (CMIT ID #134) with July 1, 2026–June 30, 2028 baseline; (v) For LEJR episodes: THA/TKA PRO‑PM (CMIT ID #1618) with July 1, 2027–July 30, 2028 baseline; (vi) For LEJR and Spinal Fusion episodes: Information Transfer PRO‑PM (CMIT ID #1797) with CY 2029 baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These measures and baseline periods are used to compute the CQS for PY5 as specified at §512.547.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigning first fiscal year MS‑DRG for fourth quarter episodes
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS assigns a first fiscal year MS‑DRG by identifying diagnosis or procedure codes that change between the first and second fiscal year of the performance year per the fiscal year final payment rule MS‑DRG definitions, for each episode with an anchor hospitalization or anchor procedure end date in the fourth quarter of a performance year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first fiscal year MS‑DRG will match the second fiscal year MS‑DRG if there are no mapping changes for an initiating MS‑DRG. CMS does not assign mapping changes for episodes with anchor hospitalization or anchor procedure end dates in the first three quarters of a performance year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of fourth quarter episodes if first fiscal year MS‑DRG not specified
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS cancels an episode with an anchor hospitalization or anchor procedure end date in the fourth quarter of a performance year, in accordance with §512.537(b), if the assigned first fiscal year MS‑DRG is not specified in §512.525(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Canceled episodes are excluded from performance year inclusion as described in §512.537(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of performance year spending using claims data timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS determines the performance year spending for each episode included in the performance year (other than canceled episodes) for each MS‑DRG/HCPCS episode type using claims data that is available 6 months after the end of the performance year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the timing for when CMS computes performance year spending for reconciliation purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of high‑cost outlier cap to performance year episode spending
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS calculates and applies the high‑cost outlier cap for performance year episode spending by applying the calculation described in §512.540(b)(4) to performance year episode spending for each MS‑DRG/HCPCS episode type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High‑cost outlier cap is defined as the 99th percentile of regional spending for a given MS‑DRG/HCPCS episode type, region, and baseline year (see definitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply adjustments to preliminary target prices to compute reconciliation target prices
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS applies the adjustments specified in §512.545 to the preliminary target prices computed in accordance with §512.540 to calculate the reconciliation target prices for each MS‑DRG/HCPCS episode type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For episodes with anchor dates in the fourth quarter, CMS calculates the reconciliation target prices for each assigned first and second fiscal year MS‑DRG/HCPCS episode type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation of reconciliation target prices across episodes
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS aggregates the reconciliation target prices computed for all episodes included in the performance year (other than canceled episodes) for each MS‑DRG/HCPCS episode type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For fourth quarter episodes, CMS aggregates reconciliation target prices for each assigned first and second fiscal year MS‑DRG/HCPCS episode type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute reconciliation differences by episode type (target minus spending)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS subtracts the performance year spending amount determined under paragraphs (c)(1) and (2) from the reconciliation target price amount determined under paragraph (c)(4) of this section for each MS‑DRG/HCPCS episode type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For fourth quarter episodes with assigned first and second fiscal year MS‑DRG/HCPCS episode types, CMS first subtracts the performance year spending from the reconciliation target amount for each assigned first and second fiscal year type, then sums values for each MS‑DRG/HCPCS episode type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sum reconciliation values across episode types to determine reconciliation amount
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS sums the values calculated under paragraph (c)(5) across all MS‑DRG/HCPCS episode types to determine the reconciliation amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aggregated sum across episode types yields the overall reconciliation amount for the participant for the performance year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cap performance year spending for low‑volume episode categories
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS caps the performance year spending amount for each MS‑DRG/HCPCS episode type to equal the reconciliation target price for episode categories where the TEAM participant did not meet the low volume threshold of at least 31 episodes during the 3‑year baseline period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low volume hospital episodes (including those where CMS caps performance year spending) are included in the CQS (per §512.547(b)) and in stop‑loss/stop‑gain threshold calculations as applied at paragraph (e) of §512.550.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of CJR‑X participant
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X participant means an acute care hospital with a CCN primary address located in the 50 United States, District of Columbia, or U.S. Territory that initiates LEJR episodes and is paid under both the IPPS and OPPS, unless it meets an exception in §512.610(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition determines which hospitals are subject to the model's requirements unless an explicit exception applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory participation and statutory exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X participants, as defined, must participate in CJR‑X, except as specified in §512.610(b). CMS excludes hospitals that: (1) are a TEAM participant as defined at §512.505, or (2) are located in the State of Maryland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants remain in CJR‑X unless they no longer meet the participant definition, CMS terminates CJR‑X, or the participant receives notice of termination under §512.165.

rubrics_metrics.name: AAPM option attestation and documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A CJR‑X participant may select the AAPM option by attesting in a form and manner and by a date specified by CMS to their use of CEHRT on an annual basis prior to the start of each performance year. A participant that selects the AAPM option must provide their CMS EHR Certification ID in a form and manner and by a date specified by CMS on an annual basis prior to the end of each performance year and must retain documentation of their attestation to CEHRT use and provide access to the documentation in accordance with §512.135.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of CEHRT use and ability to produce documentation upon request are required for AAPM election and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑AAPM assignment for failure to attest
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS assigns the CJR‑X participant to the non‑AAPM option if the CJR‑X participant does not attest in a form and manner and by a date specified by CMS to their use of CEHRT as defined in §414.1305.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely attest results in assignment to the non‑AAPM option and its consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly financial arrangements list submission and required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A CJR‑X participant with CJR‑X collaborators, collaboration agents, or downstream collaboration agents during a performance year must submit to CMS a financial arrangements list in a form and manner and by a date specified by CMS on a quarterly basis for each performance year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each collaborator the list must include name, TIN, NPI, and start/end dates of the sharing arrangement. For collaboration agents and downstream agents, the list must include the agent's name, TIN, NPI, the related collaborator or collaboration agent name and TIN, and start/end dates of distribution or downstream distribution arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly clinician engagement list submission and required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A CJR‑X participant must submit to CMS a clinician engagement list in a form and manner and by a date specified by CMS on a quarterly basis during each performance year for physicians/nonphysician practitioners/therapists who are not on the financial arrangements list but who have a contractual relationship with the participant and participate in CJR‑X activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The clinician engagement list must include for each such clinician the name, TIN, NPI, and the start date and, if applicable, the end date of the contractual relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation when no financial arrangements or clinician engagements to report
rubrics_metrics.description: A CJR‑X participant with no individuals that meet the criteria for the financial arrangements list or the clinician engagement list must attest in a form and manner and by a date specified by CMS that there are no financial arrangements or clinician engagements to report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This attestation substitutes for an empty submission and must follow CMS form/manner/date requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation retention and access for submitted lists
rubrics_metrics.description: A CJR‑X participant that submits a financial arrangements list or a clinician engagement list must retain and provide access to the documentation in accordance with §512.135.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants must be able to produce supporting documentation to CMS or its designee upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary inclusion criteria for CJR‑X
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual is a CJR‑X beneficiary if, upon admission for an anchor procedure or anchor hospitalization, the individual: (1) is enrolled in Medicare Parts A and B; (2) has Medicare as their primary payer; (3) is not eligible for Medicare on the basis of having end stage renal disease; (4) is not enrolled in any managed care plan; (5) is not covered under a United Mine Workers of America health care plan; and (6) is in an episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting all listed conditions at admission is required; failure to meet all criteria at any time during the episode results in episode cancellation per §512.630(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary notification timing and mandatory content
rubrics_metrics.description: Each CJR‑X participant must provide written notification to each CJR‑X beneficiary of his or her inclusion in the CJR‑X model prior to discharge from either the anchor hospitalization or the anchor procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The participant must be able to generate a list of beneficiaries who have received notification (including date) and provide it to CMS upon request. The notification must contain: (i) a detailed explanation of CJR‑X and how it might affect care; (ii) that the beneficiary retains freedom of choice of providers/suppliers/services; (iii) explanation of how the beneficiary can access care records and claims data through a patient portal and share Blue Button® access with caregivers; (iv) explanation of the type of beneficiary‑identifiable claims data the participant may receive; (v) a statement that existing Medicare beneficiary protections remain available (including reporting concerns to QIOs or 1‑800‑MEDICARE); and (vi) a list of CJR‑X collaborators with which the participant has a sharing arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode definition and start/end timing (90‑day episode period)
rubrics_metrics.description: Episode means all Medicare Part A and B items and services described in §512.625(b) that are furnished to a beneficiary during the time period beginning on the date of the beneficiary's admission to an anchor hospitalization or the date of the anchor procedure and ending on the 90th day following discharge or the anchor procedure (discharge/procedure date counts as day 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an anchor hospitalization for the same episode type occurs within 3 days of an anchor procedure, the anchor procedure episode is canceled and the episode start date is the anchor hospitalization date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of low‑volume hospital and consequence for caps
rubrics_metrics.description: Low‑volume hospital refers to a hospital with fewer than 31 FFS LEJR episodes during the applicable baseline period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For episode categories where the TEAM participant did not meet the low volume threshold, CMS caps performance year spending to equal the reconciliation target price and still includes those episodes in the CQS and stop‑loss/stop‑gain thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: High‑cost outlier cap definition
rubrics_metrics.description: High‑cost outlier cap refers to the 99th percentile of regional spending for a given MS‑DRG/HCPCS episode type, region, and baseline year, which is the amount at which episode spending would be capped for purposes of determining baseline and performance year episode spending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition is used when applying the cap calculation described at §512.540(b)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite Quality Score (CQS) component definitions and caps
rubrics_metrics.description: Inpatient measure composite quality score means the sum of inpatient quality measure point values capped at 20 points. Outpatient composite quality score means the sum of outpatient quality measure point values, capped at 20 points. Overall composite quality score means the sum of the weighted average of the inpatient and outpatient composite quality scores, capped at 20 points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These caps govern how quality performance is summarized and how quality adjustments may be applied to pricing/reconciliation (see related pricing and discount factor provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: CJR‑X reconciliation report requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X reconciliation report means the report prepared after each reconciliation that CMS provides to the CJR‑X participant notifying the CJR‑X participant of the outcome of the reconciliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS must prepare and provide this report to participants following reconciliation activities.
